SIAP

Structure and Interpretation of Agentic Patterns: a book in progress that teaches agent systems by building interpreters for reasoning and tool-use loops.

Status
active · manuscript in progress
Role
Author. I write the manuscript and maintain its build scripts.
Stack
agentic-systems, technical-writing, decision-theory, multi-agent-systems
Repository
Source code
Dates
Updated 2026-09-30

Live site

Problem

Agent engineering is often held together by framework defaults and prompt folklore, leaving objectives, memory, tool contracts, and failure modes under-specified.

What I built

Markdown chapters connect decision theory, planning, retrieval, safety, and multi-agent coordination to small interpreters. Python scripts build a static web reader and PDF, and audit citations and visuals.

Evidence

One hard decision

Teach by construction: each pattern is introduced as a small interpreter the reader can run and break, rather than as a framework recipe.

Where it stands

The draft is readable online and the build checks citation and visual rules on every change.

Limits

This is an unfinished draft with no external review or publisher; chapters vary in completeness and the interpreters have not been evaluated with readers.

Other projects

  • Beryl — An installable set of repository files and scripts that tell coding agents how to work in a project and check that some of those rules were actually followed.
  • Notes — this site — The site you are reading: a static build that turns my Notion study notes into public, searchable pages while keeping math, code, and nested pages intact.
  • AI Society Corpus — An interactive knowledge graph for NUS AI Society that links AI/ML study topics by prerequisites, shared tags, and backlinks.
